plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial with large, round leaves held above the water and showy, fragrant flowers on tall stalks. The flowers open in the morning and close by afternoon, and the plant is widely cultivated in ponds and water gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer, peaking July to August in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Asia, from India to China and Japan, and cultivated in ponds across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Lotus seeds have been known to germinate after more than 1,000 years of dormancy, and the leaves have a micro-textured surface that sheds water and dirt, known as the lotus effect.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy herbaceous perennial with daisy-like flowers that have drooping rosy petals around a spiky, orange-brown central cone. It thrives in prairies and sunny gardens and is a magnet for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer to early fall, at its height in July
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, widely cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: The spiky central cone gives the genus its name, from the Greek 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, and the plant has long been used in traditional Native American medicine.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and dense spikes of small, fragrant flowers. It prefers full sun and well-drained soil, and is grown in fields for essential oil and in gardens as a border plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, peaking in July
plants.location: Mediterranean region, cultivated in Provence in France, England, Bulgaria, and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning to wash, as the Romans used lavender to scent their baths.

plants.name: Callistemon citrinus
plants.description: An evergreen shrub whose cylindrical flower spikes resemble bottlebrushes, made up of long, showy red stamens. Where it grows in the Southern Hemisphere winter the plant produces sporadic blooms, and it is also popular in warm climates elsewhere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Flowers sporadically through the year, with notable blooms in winter in the Southern Hemisphere and summer in warm northern regions
plants.location: Eastern Australia, cultivated in California, the Mediterranean, South Africa, and other warm regions
plants.funFact: Bottlebrush flowers produce abundant nectar that attracts honeyeaters, lorikeets, and other nectar-feeding birds in Australia.
